title: adaptive-batching-backpressure-investigation-notes
content:
Summary:

This is an exploratory notes + runbook draft after the 2025-10-12 oncall where several hosts experienced sustained tail latency and a small cluster of worker pods hit OOMs. Pattern looked different from previous prefetched-kv-corruption incidents: memory grew gradually under moderate QPS and then spiked during a rare batch alignment event. We believe adaptive batching backpressure interacts with cache compaction and host handoffs to amplify memory usage and stall KV flush paths.

Impact observed:
- Two dedicated worker nodes OOMed (gpu-a2-small-7 & gpu-a2-small-9) between 03:24–03:35 UTC on 2025-10-12.
- ~0.8% of in-flight requests returned 503 during the incident window; error budget hit for one customer route.
- Median generation latency increased from 140ms -> 420ms for ~12 minutes.
- KV cache eviction/compaction events correlated with high write amplification in metrics (cache_bytes_written/sec spiked x6).

Why this doc exists (motivation):
- Capture the debugging timeline + signals that mattered.
- Propose concrete short-term mitigations for oncall playbook.
- Draft a longer-term runbook that explicitly covers adaptive-batching states, cache compaction, and host handoff edge cases.

Observed signals and evidence: (raw notes)
- host_metrics/gpu_mem_free: drifted down slowly then dropped at compaction boundary.
- serving_runtime/packet_queue_depth: small periodic spikes preceding latency spikes.
- batching/active_batch_sizes: modal batch size bounced between 4 and 28 when backpressure accumulation occurred.
- kv_cache/compaction_duration_ms: several long tail compactions ~1200ms (norm ~40ms).
- kernel_logs: repeated WARN "batching_backpressure: holdoff->draining" on same worker before OOM.
- trace snippets: cache-write RPCs queued on a thread that samples large prefix slices when batch alignment changes.

Timeline (concise):
- 03:19 UTC: first alert - per-host latency SLI breach.
- 03:20 UTC: ops escalated; note from oncall: "background compaction happening on several nodes".
- 03:24 UTC: host gpu-a2-small-9 OOM; process restart by kube; some requests timed out.
- 03:30 UTC: rolling pressure across the pool, second OOM on gpu-a2-small-7.
- 03:36 UTC: autoscaler briefly placed new pods; traffic redistributed.
- 03:45 UTC: metrics return to baseline once compaction queue drains and batching settles.

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Adaptive batching increases batch sizes non-monotonically during transient load; when batches align with certain request shapes it triggers large KV prefix scans to populate cache, causing memory spike.
2) Backpressure signaling currently stalls the evictor thread while waiting for drains; compaction and eviction are serialized leading to write amplification and unreclaimed memory.
3) A race during host handoff (live migration of route ownership) left temporary duplicated KV references until GC cycle, doubling memory for a short period; combined with larger batches this pushed headroom to zero.

What we tried during the incident (notes to self + commands executed):
- scaled down max batch size on the route (runtime flag override) to force smaller microbatches: curl -X POST ${ADMIN}/routes/override -d '{"route":"/generate","max_batch":8}'
- triggered manual KV compaction on suspect hosts: /opt/redwood/bin/kv-compact --host gpu-a2-small-7 --force
- quarantined one host from load to avoid cascading restarts via kubecordon/drain
- collected heap profiles (pprof) and exported to S3 key s3://ri-debug/2025-10-12/host9-pprof.heap.gz

Key debugging artifacts (where to find):
- heap profile (host9): s3://ri-debug/2025-10-12/host9-pprof.heap.gz
- trace slice with batching backpressure events: traces/2025-10-12/trace-03-23-58.json
- alert history: dashboards/alerts/latency-breach-2025-10-12

Short-term mitigations for oncall (playbook draft):
1) If latency SLO breach + rising compaction_duration_ms -> immediately reduce adaptive_batching.max_windows to 1 for affected pool (command below).
   - Admin API: POST /admin/pools/{pool}/config {"adaptive_batching.max_windows":1}
2) If a host shows compaction_duration_ms > 500ms and kernel WARNs include "holdoff->draining", cordon & drain the host and shift traffic (avoid reboot which may reintroduce pressure).
3) Temporarily raise eviction aggressiveness: kv_cache.eviction_target_ratio -> 0.65 for the pool to reduce live set size (short window, 10m).
4) If duplicated KV references suspected (observed doubled refcounts in debug info) -> run /opt/redwood/bin/kv-scan-refs --repair in maintenance window only.

Longer-term changes to implement (engineering tickets):
- Reduce coupling between adaptive batch growth and synchronous cache-population paths. Propose async prefetch path or throttled population. (JIRA-9876)
- Introduce a fast-path compaction that avoids full scan when triggered by backpressure events; metricized and toggleable. (JIRA-10102)
- Add guard rails in runtime: if batch size growth would cause estimated memory > X% of host, clamp growth and signal request-level 429 early. (Design doc link in linked_artifacts)
- Improve host-handoff protocol to avoid transient double-references during ownership transfer (detailed in GH PR linked).

Runbook draft (structured) - quick reference for oncall:
- Detection: Alert when 1) per-host mem usage increases >10% over 5m AND 2) kv_cache.compaction_duration_95 > 300ms OR batching.active_batch_size_95 > 24.
- Immediate action (first 10 minutes):
   a) Set adaptive_batching.max_windows=1 for affected pool.
   b) Cordon+drain any host with compaction_duration_ms>600ms or kernel WARNs "holdoff->draining".
   c) Increase eviction aggressiveness for 10m window.
- If >1 host OOMs: escalate to Eng SRE lead + open incident channel; temporarily disable adaptive batching for route groups with high cache-churn.
- Post-incident: collect pprof, traces, kv-metrics and drop into incident bucket; schedule follow-up postmortem within 48h.

Open questions / unknowns we should validate quickly:
- What exact request shapes produce the largest prefix-scan during cache population? Need synthetic replay harness input.
- Are compactions triggered by absolute size thresholds or by write-count thresholds in current impl? (read config code path).
- How often do host handoffs occur for this pool under normal conditions? Is there a correlation with autoscaler churn?

Immediate next steps (actionable list):
- [ ] Maya: run targeted replay for 10k requests using the trace slice to reproduce batch alignment pattern (deadline: 2025-10-22).
- [ ] Evan: add logging to compaction critical path to emit "compaction-owner" tags (deadline: 2025-10-29).
- [ ] Jordan: prepare a toggleable feature flag for async cache population prototype (prototype branch PR opened in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Rosa: update ops dashboard to include kv_cache.compaction_duration_p95 and estimated_live_set_bytes per-host (deadline: 2025-11-05).

Notes to self (informal):
- This felt different from earlier deadlocks where eviction mis-ordering caused immediate OOM. Here it's slower and emergent; good candidate for a feature-flagged mitigation rather than immediate global changes.
- Keep runbook simple: detection -> clamp batch growth -> isolate -> collect artifacts. Avoid triggering global disable unless multiple hosts OOM.

Appendix: useful commands during an incident
- Force small batches on a pool: curl -s -X POST ${ADMIN}/pools/runtime-zz/config -d '{"adaptive_batching.max_windows":1}'
- Cordon & drain host: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- Dump pprof heap: curl ${ADMIN}/debug/pprof/heap > /tmp/heap && gzip /tmp/heap && aws s3 cp /tmp/heap.gz s3://ri-debug/...

End of notes.

Unresolved: keep this doc in Drive as working draft until the prototype async-populate is validated. Mark as in_review and route to eng-serving-runtime + applied-ml; schedule an alignment meeting with Product if rewrite changes user-facing latency tradeoffs.
